OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: The organization's base permission is read, so a new member or collaborator gets read access until an owner grants more by hand; every elevated grant (the three owners' admin) is an explicit assignment. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main; its only bypass actor (the maintainer) holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the review while merging a pull request and never a direct push, so a direct push to main is refused for everyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset carries a deletion rule (plus non_fast_forward) with no bypass actor, and classic protection sets allow_deletions false, so main cannot be deleted by anyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at both the organization and the repository, and GitHub Actions cannot approve pull requests; every workflow also declares permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets `permissions: contents: read` at the top and elevates per job only for what the job does: `id-token`/`attestations` for publishing and attesting, `security-events` for CodeQL and Scorecard, `pull-requests` for the review, `issues` for the two sentinels that open one, `contents: write` only in the release job. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/.github/workflows

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`; untrusted event fields and dispatch inputs reach `run:` steps only through `env:` variables, and zizmor's template-injection audit runs in the required lint check. The review job runs on `issue_comment` with the default branch checked out and is gated by the `CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED` variable. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request trigger, which gives a fork's code no secrets and a read-only token; the one job holding a secret on a pull request (the review) runs only when the head repository is this repository, and the comment-triggered job checks out the default branch, not the pull request's code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: Collaborator input reaches pipelines as workflow_dispatch inputs, which are passed to steps through env: rather than interpolated into scripts (zizmor's template-injection audit enforces it) and checked by the step that consumes them, e.g. pypi-install.yml waits for the index to serve exactly the version named. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/pypi-install.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D) set by a signed v* tag; release.yml's version-check job refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name (sdist, wheel, `<name>-<version>.cdx.json`, `<tag>.intoto.jsonl`), and the attestation binds each to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS-only; PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle, so a tampered download fails verification. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: Every release carries CHANGELOG.md's entry (every change) and RELEASE_NOTES.md's (what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included); the GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Pipelines take dependencies through uv from PyPI against the committed uv.lock (`--locked`; the release build pins its build requirements with `UV_BUILD_CONSTRAINT`), and third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA (organization `sha_pinning_required`); the organization's own reusable workflows are called at `@main` on purpose. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and the GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle (`<tag>.intoto.jsonl`, or `<tag>.attestation.jsonl` on releases up to v2026.9.29) whose subjects are each asset's SHA-256; the tag is signed, as the tag-integrity ruleset requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and its push protection are enabled, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused; the detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run against .secrets.baseline in the required lint check for credentials GitHub does not recognise. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: The organization's policy, https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940 : a secret is an environment secret that only the owners can reach, any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md, a secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly in a "Secrets review <year>" issue. tests/secrets_test.py reads every store and refuses an unrecorded entry.

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is docs/source/guide.rst, a task-oriented guide whose examples tests/docs_examples_test.py runs, plus the API reference, published at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what a report needs; SECURITY.md routes a vulnerability away from the public tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md and RELEASING.md give the gh attestation verify command (with --repo and --signer-workflow, or --bundle offline) for the release assets, and RELEASING.md gives the rebuild-from-tag check that reproduces the sdist. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verification command pins the authoring identity: `--repo` names this repository and `--signer-workflow` the organization's `reusable-build.yml` (`reusable-attest.yml` or `release.yml` for older releases, as SECURITY.md lists), so an attestation from any other workflow or repository is refused. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions* states that a release stops receiving security updates as soon as the next one is published, since only the latest is supported and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: Each runtime dependency's reason is written beside it in pyproject.toml; dependencies are obtained from PyPI through uv and pinned in uv.lock, and tracked by Dependabot's weekly grouped updates with a seven-day cooldown, as the standard's sections 1 and 11 state. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer (the only bypass actor) and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments, with the command that reads them back; the tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: an issue first, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution meets: an issue behind it, one subject, the lint gate (ruff select ALL, strict mypy), line and branch coverage at 100%, a signed commit, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46 : a grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there.

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off status check, so a pull request cannot merge unless every commit carries a Signed-off-by: trailer (the DCO assertion) from its author. Commits made in the web interface are signed off automatically (web_commit_signoff_required is on). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: The release is pure Python, with nothing compiled; even so, every release attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM (<name>-<version>.cdx.json) generated from the built wheel, listing both files' SHA-256, the license and the declared dependencies, and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: Classic protection on main requires the listed status checks with strict up-to-date; enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge that lands without them is a manual bypass, which is the case the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed: the only non-text blobs are Bitcoin-serialized test data and fuzz seeds; the lint gate's check-added-large-files and the package-content policy keep builds out of the tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: The binary files are Bitcoin blocks, transactions and P2P messages used as test vectors and fuzz seeds: each is decodable by the library itself, and the vendored ones are pinned to their source in tests/_data/README.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The documented policy is 100% line and branch coverage (standard section 8; CONTRIBUTING.md), so a change adding untested functionality fails the required test check; pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: The ruleset asks for one approving review, but the maintainer is its bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval as everyday practice, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the components, their layering and every place the software reaches outside the process, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module (ruff's D rules require them, and a docs test fails when a shipped module is missing from the reference); CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on the repository, as SECURITY.md commits to; the first, GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, was published on 2026-10-03. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3120-L3135 : the CycloneDX SBOM published with each release carries a vulnerabilities array, built from the tree's .github/vex.toml, with analysis.state not_affected, a CycloneDX justification and the reason for each vulnerability judged not to affect the release. No vulnerability is judged so today, so no tree keeps the file; the alignment suite (tests/vex_test.py) refuses a Dependabot alert dismissed as not affecting without its entry.

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909 : every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml, and an exception is a purl named there with its reason.

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160 : release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job, and an advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX document states as not affecting it.

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: Every pull request runs the Dependency review job (policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909), and the job is a required status check on main ("lint / Dependency review" in branch protection), so a pull request that violates the policy cannot merge.

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL (bandit's S rules included), and every finding is fixed or suppressed with a # noqa and a reason at its site; zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the bandit S rules, strict mypy, zizmor on workflows, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding unless suppressed in place with a reason; CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization now has three owners with admin rights on every repository -- fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, confirmed live via `gh api "orgs/btclib-org/members?role=admin"` -- so any two of the three can create and close issues, accept changes and cut a release within a week of the third becoming unavailable, per GOVERNANCE.md's *Continuity*. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: btclib is a library with no user interface, so accessibility practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every push to main and every pull request, and its aggregate job is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Pure-Python source is used directly (uv_build, no compilation step), so there is nothing whose bit-for-bit regeneration to test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies the rebuilt file against the release's own PyPI attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Besides the maintainer, no one has committed code to this repository since 2023, so the project does not show a bus factor of 2. The three organization owners hold admin access, and one of them reviewed security in issue #2450. The project does not claim a second knowledgeable maintainer yet.

code_of_conduct.justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md lives in btclib-org/.github and is shown by GitHub as this repository's code of conduct through the organization's default community-health-file inheritance, confirmed via the repository's community-profile API. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] selects every ruff rule family (`select = ["ALL"]`) with a documented `ignore` list, and [tool.mypy] runs in strict mode; CONTRIBUTING.md's lint-gate section names both and the commands that enforce them on every contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as required pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: Only one contributor is significant today: the maintainer has 1604 commits in the last 12 months and every other person has three or fewer.

copyright_per_file.justification: Every source file (.py, .c, .h) opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: btclib implements the Bitcoin protocol, whose consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes; another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. The curve and hash agility is in btclib-ecc, which btclib depends on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: btclib calls libraries for its primitives: curve arithmetic and signature schemes from btclib-ecc, BIP324's ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 from cryptography, hashes from hashlib. It writes only what Bitcoin's specifications build on them (MuHash3072, the BIP324 key schedule). Its RIPEMD-160 is Bitcoin Core's own Python copy, used only where hashlib has none. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_credential_agility.justification: btclib is a library with no configuration file or credential store: a private key or password is a caller-supplied function parameter, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_keylength.justification: The keys btclib works with are secp256k1 keys, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030; BIP324's ciphers use 256-bit keys. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_pfs.justification: btclib.p2p.bip324 implements BIP324's key schedule: the session keys come from an ElligatorSwift ECDH over the key pair BIP324 makes fresh for each connection, and both ciphers rekey every 224 packets. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/p2p/bip324.py

crypto_published.justification: btclib imports its curve arithmetic from btclib_ecc, which calls btclib-secp256k1 (bindings to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1) wherever a call can use them and otherwise runs Python arithmetic; SECURITY.md states when each applies and `btclib_ecc.curves.is_libsecp256k1_serving()` tells a caller which. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_random.justification: btclib draws randomness only from Python's `secrets` module (the BMS nonce, the transaction input and output shuffle); ECDSA nonces are deterministic (RFC 6979). Key, mnemonic and nonce generation is in btclib_ecc and btclib-wallet, which hold their own entries. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib

crypto_tls12.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_used_network.justification: btclib does not talk to the network at all -- docs/source/guide.rst states this explicitly as one of the things the library will not do -- so there are no network communications for a secure-protocol choice to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_verification_private.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_weaknesses.justification: btclib uses SHA-256 (BIP340, BIP327, RFC 6979); the only SHA-1 is Bitcoin script's `OP_SHA1`, which the protocol requires and which is flagged `usedforsecurity=False`. Curve schemes and ECIES are btclib_ecc's; SECURITY.md documents where a secret crosses into the Python fallback. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dco.justification: Every commit carries a Signed-off-by: trailer from its author (the DCO assertion): main requires the lint / Sign-off status check, which refuses a pull request with a commit lacking it, and CONTRIBUTING.md says so. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot's version-update and security-update ecosystems are configured in .github/dependabot.yml, dependabot_security_updates is enabled on the repository, and CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard run on a schedule as well. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md already carries and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, on the line the organization standard reserves for it, alongside the Scorecard badge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_basics.justification: Some documentation basics file contents found.

documentation_current.justification: The docs build is gated in CI (docs.yml, `-W -n`) and the API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings on every release, so a documentation defect against the current release fails the gate rather than going unnoticed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_quick_start.justification: docs/source/guide.rst is a task-oriented quick-start whose examples run under tests/docs_examples_test.py, so a stale example fails the suite rather than misleading a reader. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is deliberately not; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* section states in detail what a user can and cannot expect -- constant-time behaviour, key zeroization, which operations delegate to libsecp256k1 and which run the pure-Python fallback -- referencing the assurance case as the threat model those promises are written against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: The suite runs under pytest, which rewrites `assert` statements, and the fuzz and mutation jobs run the library with assertions enabled (no `-O`). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model, the maintainer's bypass and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: The project site https://btclib.org/btclib/ is served over HTTPS behind Cloudflare and answers Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security; check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/btclib/

hardening.justification: ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the flake8-bandit (S) family, so a hardening-relevant defect -- an unsafe deserialization, a weak temp-file, a shell injection -- is caught at the lint gate rather than only in review; CodeQL runs the same search at a different granularity on every push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section argues how each principle applies, against ARCHITECTURE.md's layer boundaries; SECURITY.md's *Limitations* section applies the same argument to where a secret meets the curve. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: The package is on PyPI, so `pip install btclib` (or `pip uninstall`) is the commonly-used convention for installing and removing it; README.md gives the exact command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's repository-specific "The environment and the gates" section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions (site-packages, or DESTDIR-honouring behaviour inherited from pip itself); there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP (pyupgrade) and FA rule families run at `select = ["ALL"]` and flag deprecated stdlib and typing constructs; the deps-latest and deps-oldest sentinels exercise the supported interpreter range weekly, so a newly deprecated API is caught close to its deprecation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: btclib produces no end-user text to localize; its output is hex, addresses and error messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: The assurance case argues how each common implementation weakness (CWE-20, 209, 248, 330/338, 347, 502, 755, 843 and others) is countered in this tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: The primary developer wrote the assurance case, which argues each secure-design principle against the architecture. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

license_location.justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE>.

license_per_file.justification: Every source file (.py, .c, .h) states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported, per SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*; the upgrade path is documented instead -- RELEASING.md requires a breaking-changes check (`griffe check`) against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md carries the resulting before/after list for every source-breaking change. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: Every pull request merged in the last six months that fixes a bug in src/ also changes tests/, measured 2026-09-25. The suite's 100% line-and-branch coverage floor also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

release_notes.justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md>.

release_notes_vulns.justification: The release notes name each advisory a release fixes by its GHSA id, for example v2026.10.4 and GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md>. [osps_do_02_01]

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member (organization setting two_factor_requirement_enabled = true), so nobody without 2FA can change a repository. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* section names the maintainer, the owners, repository administrators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot and Dependabot, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: Security review of 2026-09-30 by pmazzocchi, an owner of the organization other than the maintainer: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues/2450 . It pins its scope to a commit, checks every claim and trust boundary of ASSURANCE_CASE.md (the security requirements and boundary, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md), states what it did not cover, and files each finding as an issue.

signed_releases.justification: The v2026.10.4 tag is a signed, GitHub-verified annotated tag; RELEASING.md documents how a release is cut and signed and SECURITY.md how to verify it, and the PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/tag/v2026.10.4

sites_password_security.justification: The project sites (GitHub, PyPI, Read the Docs, btclib.org) store no passwords of this project's; authentication is theirs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution; 25 such issues were open at some time between 2025-10-04 and 2026-10-04. The organization's standard requires one in every 12 months (README section 10). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification:
https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/test.yml
The test suite covers virtually the whole code base, a floor the build enforces, and it answers to vectors their authors publish: the BIPs' and the SLIPs' own, Bitcoin Core's script, transaction, sighash and key-encoding files, HWI's, trezor's for BIP39 and SLIP39, and Appendix A.2 of RFC 6979. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to the upstream commit it was copied from, and says whether the two still match — including the few vectors that are btclib's own, having no upstream.

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (`branch = true` under `[tool.coverage.run]`) and the 100% gate includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_policy_mandated.justification: The 100% coverage floor described in CONTRIBUTING.md's testing section is a de facto and enforced written policy: a line of new functionality with no covering test fails the CI gate outright, `fail_under = 100.0` admitting no exception. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100.0`, gated on every pull request by the coverage job; the suite is gated well above the 80% floor this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (`fail_under = 100.0` under `[tool.coverage.report]`) on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100%-coverage requirement as part of how a change is proposed, which states the same policy tests_documented_added asks for: new functionality is not accepted without a covering test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: The ruleset asks for one approving review, but the maintainer is its bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval as everyday practice, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review [osps_qa_07_01]

updateable_reused_components.justification: Reused components are either standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped weekly by Dependabot and the deps-latest sentinel, which runs the full suite against the upgrade before it lands. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml

version_semver.justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing

version_tags_signed.justification: Every release tag from v2026.8.21 on is a signed, verified annotated tag, and the `tag-integrity` ruleset (`required_signatures` on `refs/tags/v*`, no bypass) refuses an unsigned one; earlier tags predate the rule. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tags

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: The reporter of GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, pmazzocchi, is credited as finder on the published advisory: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r

vulnerability_report_response.justification: A vulnerability was reported privately on 2026-09-30 and fixed and published within 3 days (GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, patched in 2026.10.4), well inside the 14-day response limit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* section documents the private channel (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see it, and how a CVE can be requested; private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository (`gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib/private-vulnerability-reporting` answers enabled). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: warning are not tolerated: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are required, zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again in the lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
